presenting_complaint: abdominal pain, Generalized tonic–clonic seizures, seizures, Generalized body convulsions
symptoms_absent: no abnormal lesions in brain MRI
no elevated lactate levels after exercise

candidate_mimics.evidence_sentence: A urinary tract infection was considered, and after receiving corresponding treatment, the abdominal pain and vomiting resolved within two weeks.
His proximal upper limb weakness was assessed as motor axonal neuropathy, raising an initial high suspicion of Guillain-Barré syndrome (GBS).

candidate_mimics.diagnosis: mitochondrial encephalomyopathy with lactic acidosis and stroke-like episodes (MELAS)
candidate_mimics.evidence_sentence: mitochondrial encephalomyopathy with lactic acidosis and stroke-like episodes (MELAS) and AIP were considered as possible diagnoses.

final_diagnosis_evidence: positive PBG in a urine sample, which was tested using the qualitative Watson-Schwartz method at PUMC, along with genetic testing that identified a c.445C > T (R149X) mutation in the HMBS gene.
vignette: A 26-year-old male presents with Generalized body convulsions, Bilateral upper limb weakness, Generalized tonic–clonic seizures, Recurrent vomiting, Profuse sweating, Hypertension, Sinus tachycardia, Hyponatremia.
ollama_review_notes: Acute intermittent porphyria is a diagnosis of exclusion. The presence of seizures, neurological symptoms, and specific laboratory findings (e.g., tea-colored urine) support this diagnosis.
